title: Bank Rate on 1 January 1856 and on each day it changed, 1856-1858
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'D1. Official Interest Rates' (Bank Rate 1833-1972 ...), daily
series: date (ISO 8601): 1 January 1856 and each day on which the rate differs from the previous row of the sheet; bank_rate: the new rate, per cent a year
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England and to the authors of the series.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb (the copy used for boe_millennium_gb_1790_1830 and boe_millennium_gb_1822_1827_monthly). The script checks the heading of the date column and of the Bank Rate column. The sheet dates the rise to 10 per cent 12 November 1857; D. M. Evans (1859) says the rate was raised to 10 per cent on 11 November (marx_facts row ev_rate10). The chapter follows the Bank's table and records the difference in its notes on sources.
citation: Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017), sheet D1
